title: Declarative Swatch Bridge and Variant Governance Playbook
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Create a playbook and reference artifacts that define a declarative swatch bridging strategy between old console color variables and the new adaptive swatch tokens, and a governance model for component variants across dashboards, rollout rails, and cost views.
background: Multiple teams have diverged on color usage and component variants when migrating panels and metric cards to the new compact density. There are duplicated figma styles, inconsistent hover/focus states in rollout rails, and mismatch between runtime token names and figma swatch names. This causes visual regressions and slows rollouts that need coordinated design + engineering updates.
goals: Provide a one-page canonical mapping from legacy color variables to the new adaptive swatch tokens
Define rules for variant naming and composition that are executable in Figma components and match runtime prop names
Create a lightweight governance workflow for approving token changes with impact analysis across Console dashboards and cost widgets
Ship a prototype Figma page that demonstrates migration of three representative components: Data KPI card, Canary rollout rail, and Cost breakdown table
acceptance_criteria: Canonical mapping table published in the Design Drive and linked from the Console design library
Figma prototype with annotated instances for the three representative components is available and reviewed by PMs and Eng
Checklist for token change impact analysis integrated into the design review template
Two cross-functional workshops completed with notes and action items tracked in the parent ticket
out_of_scope: Deep runtime migration work (engine changes to runtime token resolution) and billing-backend cost-model adjustments are out of scope and will be tracked as engineering dependences.
decisions_made: Adopt a declarative naming pattern: <surface>.<state>.<intent> (e.g., panel.bg.default, pill.border.focus)
Introduce an automated mapping CSV that can be ingested by the console build to generate a compatibility layer (design artifact only; engineering ticket required for ingestion)
Use 'adaptive' prefix for tokens intended to vary by density or contrast (adaptive.surface.card) to avoid ambiguity
Reserve legacy variable names in the figma library with a deprecation note for two releases before removal

Eng - Nora Singh: CSV is useful, but we need a separate eng ticket for runtime compatibility import; flagged dependency ENG-33421
Accessibility - Priya Rao: Some adaptive tokens failed AA for small text; recommended contrast surface adjustments and a high-contrast token set

migration_steps: 1) Publish canonical mapping and update Figma library tokens with 'legacy' deprecation notes
2) Run design-to-runtime gap analysis and produce ENG ingestion ticket for CSV import
3) Migrate component instances in Figma to use adaptive tokens via instance swap plugin
4) Run visual diff snapshots for dashboards and cost views in staging once runtime mapping available
5) Deprecate legacy variables after two successful release cycles
accessibility_notes: High-contrast variant required for metric labels under 12px
Hover and focus states must maintain at least 3:1 contrast ratio against background for non-text UI components
Provide alternate tokens for customers who enable 'increased contrast' in Console settings
risks: Engineering bandwidth: ingestion ticket delayed could block runtime verification
Scope creep: expanding prototype to more components without freeze increases review time
Naming collisions: unintuitive token names can lead to incorrect runtime mapping and visual regressions
next_steps: Address PM feedback about cost-view impact and annotate mapping CSV with 'semantic impact' column
Coordinate with ENG-33421 to create acceptance criteria for runtime import
Finalize governance workflow and add to design-review checklist
Run a 45-minute cross-functional sign-off session week of 2026-03-15
notes_for_engineering: Provide a lightweight CSV ingestion API that accepts columns: legacy_name, new_token, intent, impact_level
Support reserved legacy variables for two release cycles before deletion
